artifacts.purpose: Installed fleet adapter discovery/readiness state consumed by Start-AgentSwitchboard.ps1 and startup reporting.
Canonical installed Windows PowerShell operator implementation. Pair with fleet-state and invoke through pwsh for readiness or bounded sprint execution.
CMD compatibility shim for the installed PowerShell implementation. Presence or execution is not a prerequisite for core readiness on policy-restricted Windows.
Machine-readable bootstrap/repair result including step statuses, agents, install root, error state, and Hermes skipped/blocked evidence when deferred.
Human diagnostic transcript for bootstrap/repair attempts, including shell/setup details and Hermes deferral evidence.
Machine-readable local adapter readiness; does not prove provider authentication or hosted response.
English-language startup/readiness report with next actions per agent.
Launch-time route evidence for provider-specific paths such as DeepSeek through OpenCode.

stateGates.condition: exactly one of fleet-state or installed-operator-implementation exists
stateGates.requiredAction: run repository-owned setup in repair/reuse mode; do not fabricate the missing surface

stateGates.condition: fleet-state and installed-operator-implementation exist AND the optional installed-operator-launcher is missing or Windows denies CMD shim execution (including exit 5)
stateGates.requiredAction: invoke installed Start-AgentSwitchboard.ps1 through pwsh; do not rerun setup solely for the CMD shim

stateGates.condition: fleet-state and installed-operator-implementation exist AND Hermes is unavailable/skipped/blocked while core setup did not fail
stateGates.requiredAction: record Hermes as TBD/deferred, prove current readiness through PowerShell, and continue only with observed READY non-Hermes adapters
run PowerShell -ListAgents/readiness before choosing an agent

stateGates.condition: readiness output reports requested adapter ready or verification-required
stateGates.requiredAction: apply target-repository cleanliness, prompt, provider, and stop-condition gates before sprint launch

compatibilitySurfaces.name: installed CMD shim
compatibilitySurfaces.rule: The shim delegates to the PowerShell implementation. When Windows policy blocks the shim, use the PowerShell implementation directly and preserve the shim failure as boundary evidence.

optionalDependencies.name: Hermes
optionalDependencies.rule: Hermes may not block core autoconfig. Preserve setup evidence and repair Hermes later in a separate bounded lane.

namingConventions: Generated setup and readiness evidence is local-operational and untracked.
Timestamped run directories/files are producer-owned; agents resolve them through this registry or producer output instead of guessing paths.
Hermes deferred/TBD is recorded in the setup summary and readiness report; do not create an ad-hoc tracked machine-state file.
Do not copy machine-specific paths, credentials, provider secrets, or raw runtime logs into tracked milestone docs.
The PowerShell operator implementation plus fleet state are the installed readiness authority; the CMD shim is a compatibility surface.
A launcher path is an installed surface, not proof of readiness by itself.
